chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Naḍr al-Armanī, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a group who are on a journey, and one of them dies while there is among them a junub, and they have only a small amount of water, enough for only one of the two. Which of them should be attended to first? He said: The junub performs ghusl, and the deceased is left, because this is an obligation and that is a sunnah (prophetic tradition).

So the proper way of reconciling these two reports is what we have already presented in the first report equally; moreover, it has been narrated that when the deceased and the junub are together, the deceased is given ghusl and the junub performs tayammum.

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state in which this ruling takes place
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: here, a non-obligatory prescribed practice in contrast to an obligation
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory act with legal priority
key_terms.مَاءٌ قَلِيلٌ: a small amount of water insufficient for both needs
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: a deceased person requiring ritual washing
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: performs tayammum as a substitute purification

ai.seo_question: If there is only enough water for either a deceased person’s ghusl or a junub’s ghusl during travel, which one takes priority?
ai.summary: This report addresses a jurisprudential ruling concerning limited water during travel when both a deceased person and a junub are present. It presents one ruling giving priority to the junub’s ghusl as an obligation over the washing of the deceased, while also noting another transmitted ruling in which the deceased is washed and the junub performs tayammum.
